checks.finding: REQ-004 defines Resolver Evidence's diagnostics[] as {id, detail, severity: "block"|"warn"}, recording 'every diagnostic-worthy condition this invocation encountered, not only the first/fatal one.' But REQ-002's entire 16-row diagnostic-id taxonomy is framed exclusively as fail-closed Block conditions ('Enumerate every condition under which the Resolver refuses to produce...'), and Edge Cases states 'There is no longer an accepted-WARN case anywhere in this feature's own evaluation model.' No requirement, edge case, or AC ever describes a scenario producing a diagnostics[] entry with severity:"warn" (as opposed to "block"), or its cardinality relationship to a same-id "block" summary entry (e.g. for dsl-warn-on-matched-capability, which REQ-004's own no-short-circuit language implies could be recorded per offending branch). Two compliant implementations could diverge (one never emitting "warn", another emitting one "warn" entry per branch plus a "block" summary), producing non-byte-identical diagnostics[] arrays for identical input and undermining REQ-005's byte-identical guarantee and AC-021's validator conformance rules for this branch. No fixture in REQ-006's matrix or AC-027 exercises severity:"warn" specifically.

(1) requirements.md REQ-006 states its future suites cover 'the eleven items design.md's own Test Strategy fixes at contract level,' in the same clause explaining this is 'expanded from an earlier revision's eight — new items 9/10 add the metamorphic-completeness and live-caller-contract suites' (8+2=10, not 11 — an internal arithmetic contradiction). acceptance-tests.md restates the identical fact set twice as 'ten suites' ('design.md's own Test Strategy names ten suites...' / '...keeping the suite count at ten'), directly contradicting REQ-006's own headline 'eleven.' A future tasks.md author following requirements.md vs. acceptance-tests.md would schedule a different number of Test-Strategy-suite-authoring tasks. (2) REQ-002's project-context-validation-failed row requires the Resolver to detect that '--config's target file exists but fails Epic A1's own content-schema validation surface' — but the Dependencies section states canonicalize-sdd-yaml's CLI 'is the ONLY path from YAML bytes to a structure this feature's Resolver ever uses,' and investigation.md INV-007 confirms that CLI is a pure byte-canonicalizer ('emitting canonical UTF-8 bytes... on stdout and nothing else') with no content-schema-validation capability; no other Epic A1 validator CLI is named anywhere in this package, unlike every sibling row (e.g. registry-validation-failed names validate-capability-registry explicitly). This makes one of AC-010's own sixteen independently-fixture-tested Block conditions impossible to implement as specified without inventing a dependency this package's own Dependencies section forbids — an impossible acceptance criterion, the calibration's own Critical anchor.

REQ-002's output-schema-validation-failed row and AC-012 jointly establish two materially different observable behaviors for this one diagnostic-id: if Resolver Evidence itself is the failing artifact, 'this invocation writes NOTHING to any live path, not even a best-effort... Evidence instance' (B3); if any other staged artifact (Facet Manifest/Capability Summary/Context Projection) fails instead, Resolver Evidence is still written recording the diagnostic (REQ-002's general 'still written on every Block' rule, only two named exceptions). AC-010/TEST-010 requires only 'one fixture per REQ-002/design.md diagnostic-id row (sixteen total)... each independently triggerable' — satisfiable by a single fixture covering only one of these two sub-cases. No AC in acceptance-tests.md requires both the 'Evidence itself fails' and 'a non-Evidence artifact fails while Evidence still publishes' sub-cases to each have a dedicated fixture, so a test-author following AC-010 literally could ship a suite that never exercises the more common, non-Evidence-artifact-fails sub-case's own distinct writes-Evidence-only behavior.

The Assumptions section names exactly three residual latent risks (sibling A1-A3 contracts changing before Phase 2 begins; the resolve-project-context.* protected-suffix reservation's live status; SKILL.md's unprotected status) and each carries an explicit fallback procedure exercised if the assumption fails to hold at implementation-start time (e.g. 'the future implementation task re-verifies the file's then-current protection status before choosing a direct unprotected-first-then-register sequencing... instead of the content-population-only human-copy this package assumes'). The one genuine open cross-epic gap this feature depends on — Epic A2's Registry schema lacking a required_lite_checks source (investigation.md INV-019) — is not left as a silent assumption but is recorded as an explicit, owned prerequisite for Epic A6 in both Dependencies and Risks, with owner, scope, and migration stated.

Roles and Permissions fixes a clear, testable irreversible-change boundary: the Resolver script family's own code content is human-copy-gated ('specs/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/human-copy/' -> apply-human-copy, 'never a direct agent write to the live path,' investigation.md INV-003), strictly distinguished from live per-Feature artifacts which are 'agent-writable-only-via-the-Resolver... never hand-edited.' Security Boundaries further fixes that 'the Resolver never writes to any *.approval.json sidecar, any sdd/.approved-context/ anchor, or guard-invariants.json itself... it never participates in the approval-sidecar workflow itself,' explicitly delegating human-approval workflow to Epic A1's own already-Passed mechanism, while REQ-002's own 16-row fail-closed Block taxonomy (independently fixture-tested via AC-010 through AC-014 and AC-038-054) is itself the in-scope governance mechanism preventing an under-specified artifact from silently publishing.

Two findings above directly block a clean handoff to implementation-policy review: (1) project-context-validation-failed (REQ-002) names no callable mechanism, and the Dependencies section's own 'canonicalize-sdd-yaml... is the ONLY path' restriction rules out the one tool this package does name — a design reviewer inheriting this package would have to invent which Epic A1 surface satisfies this already-tested (AC-010) diagnostic, a product/contract decision this Phase 1 package claims to have already fixed rather than a design-phase architectural choice; (2) REQ-006's own 'eleven items' test-suite count directly contradicts acceptance-tests.md's twice-stated 'ten suites,' so a downstream task author would schedule a different Test Strategy suite count depending on which document they follow, with nothing in this package flagging which number is authoritative. Both require a product-level decision this specification claims to have already closed, not an implementation-styling choice appropriate for the next gate to originate.
